article.title: Moving from Windows to Mac: separate file sorting from cleanup
article.primaryIntent: Help a former 4-Organizer Ultra user decide what to preserve, organize and inspect after moving to Mac, without treating file rearrangement as reclaimed space.
outline: Separate three jobs: organizing originals, reviewing disposable data, observing recurring growth.
Inventory before rearranging: preserve backups and project/media folder relationships; large is not disposable.
Explain 4-Organizer's Windows sorting preview, exclusions and rollback limits from official docs, not pretend to run it on Mac.
On Mac, inspect categories and app/tool ownership before approving cleanup; distinguish size, Trash moves and available-space change.
Use a decision checklist: need automatic file sorting, exact cleanup review, or ongoing investigation? Breathing Room is not documented as a general file-sorter replacement.
Bounded recommendation with affiliation and preview/runtime/hosted-service caveats; built-in Mac approaches need Apple documentation before procedural claims.
article.distinctness: Workflow separation for a platform switch, not the comparison matrix expanded. No separate alternatives doorway page.
article.interactionHandoff: Non-mutating three-job decision checklist (sort originals / review cleanup / investigate growth); no filesystem access, promises or calculator savings.
article.visualPlacement: Space example-data image after lead; permission-cleared competitor sorting/review app UI beside workflow explanation. Current link-only candidates do not satisfy this requirement.

comparison.title: 4-Organizer Ultra and Breathing Room: Windows care or Mac inspection?
comparison.primaryIntent: Concise platform-first decision for a Mac switcher, not a Windows benchmark or feature-parity replacement claim.
comparison.conclusion: For an existing Windows file-sorting workflow, 4-Organizer documents previews and rollbacks that this research does not establish in Breathing Room. For a Mac storage-investigation workflow, Breathing Room, which we build, is relevant only with explicit preview, Python, notarization and hosted-assistance caveats.
